title: Persistence Basics
description: Learn to persist React Query cache to survive page reloads and browser sessions.

data.text: Cache persistence stores the React Query cache in a durable storage medium so that data survives page reloads, browser restarts, and even temporary offline periods. Without persistence, every refresh clears the cache and forces a loading state. Persistence lets your app show cached data instantly while validating freshness in the background.

data.title: Mobile UX Win
data.text: Persistence is especially valuable for mobile users on unreliable networks. Showing cached data instantly while validating in the background feels much faster than a blank loading screen, and works even when the user is completely offline.
Choosing the right storage backend depends on your data size, performance requirements, and browser support needs. React Query ships with persisters for the most common options.

terms.definition: A wrapper around a storage API that serializes and deserializes the React Query cache.
Restoring the query cache from persisted storage when the app starts.
A caching strategy where cached data is served immediately while a background refetch updates it.

data.text: The `@tanstack/query-sync-storage-persister` package provides a `createSyncStoragePersister` utility that works with any synchronous storage API â€” localStorage and sessionStorage included. Wrap your app with `PersistQueryClientProvider` and the cache is automatically persisted and hydrated.

data.text: When to Persist and When Not To

data.title: Good Candidates for Persistence
items: User-specific data that rarely changes: profile, settings, preferences.
Reference data: countries, categories, static lookups used across the app.
Offline-first applications: PWAs, mobile web apps, internal tools.
Form drafts and unsaved user input that should survive a page reload.

data.title: Avoid Persisting
items: Auth tokens or session credentials â€” use secure HTTP-only cookies.
Highly volatile data that changes every few seconds.
Large media blobs or binary files.
Any data containing PII that must not persist on the device.

data.title: Security First
data.text: Do not persist sensitive data like auth tokens or personal information in localStorage. It is accessible to any script on the page and persists across sessions. Use secure, HTTP-only cookies for sensitive credentials.

data.title: Exercise: Add Persistence to a Todo App
data.description: Add cache persistence to a simple todo app that uses React Query. The app should show cached todos instantly on reload, even offline.
steps: Create a QueryClient with a cacheTime of 1 hour.
Create a persister using localStorage with the key 'todo-app-cache'.
Test by adding a todo, reloading the page, and verifying the todo still appears.
data.expectedOutcome: Todos load instantly from cache on reload, then validate freshness in the background.

items.question: Does persistence replace the need for an API?
items.answer: No. Persistence is a cache layer on top of your API. It stores data locally for instant loads and offline use, but the authoritative data still lives on your server.

items.question: What happens when the persisted cache is stale?
items.answer: The app renders with stale data immediately, then React Query background refetches in the background. The UI updates when fresh data arrives. This is the stale-while-revalidate pattern.

items.question: Can I persist only specific queries?
items.answer: Yes. Use the persistOptions.filter callback in PersistQueryClientProvider to selectively persist queries based on their query key.

data.title: Persistence Basics Key Points
points: Persistence stores the cache beyond page reloads and browser restarts.
localStorage is simple and synchronous but limited in size.
Persist only non-sensitive, relatively static data.
Combine persistence with background refetching for freshness.
data.takeaway: Persistence is the foundation of offline-capable React Query applications.
